newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDIC's Helfer to remain vocal on bank issues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDIC's Helfer to remain vocal on bank issues.

text.p: Ricki Helfer, outgoing chairman of the Federal Deposit Insurance Fund, said Friday she plans to continue speaking out on bank issues after leaving her current position in June.

Addressing thousands of bankers gathered here for the annual Independent Bankers Association of America meeting, Helfer pledged to remain a participant in the current debate over reforming archaic U.S. banking laws.
"I'm not going to disappear from view," Helfer said to loud applause. "I'm going to continue to speak out."

"I have no expectation that I will lose my voice after June 1," she added before leaving with a dozen roses and a standing ovation from the bankers, representatives of the country's smaller, community banks.

Helfer, who has not announced her future plans, shocked the banking industry when she revealed earlier this month her planned resignation. Helfer said she was stepping down to spend more time with her family and because she had accomplished the goals she had set out for herself when she took the job two and a half years ago. --Aaron Pressman((202-898-8312))
